papers.title: Intersection Cohomology Without Spaces
papers.license: Official SIAM publication: CC BY 4.0; arXiv v2 license link also CC BY 4.0.

coverage.read_body: All body sections 1-9, PDF pp. 1-17; bibliography inspected for cited and forthcoming items, not a reading of the referenced papers.
integrated_sections: 3: P-kernels, KLS recursion, matroid KL and Z polynomials
4.2-4.4: poset sheaves, flabbiness, minimal graded free covers
5: fans, minimal extension sheaves, Karu dimension realization and square example
7: equivariant Mobius algebra, flat-by-flat module construction and four conditions identifying KL/Z polynomials
8.2: top-heaviness theorem and complete linear-algebra reduction from an embedding and hard Lefschetz
proof_detail: 01C7 supplies an explicit algebraic induction for KLS existence and uniqueness.
01CO and 01D1 are labelled proof routes; Hodge-theoretic vanishing is an input, not proved.
01CR gives the linear-algebra implication from a module embedding and hard Lefschetz to top-heaviness.

sections: 6.1: labeled type-A moment graphs, incidence sheaves and boundary-image/minimal-cover recursion
6.2: explicit rank-one moment-graph/Soergel comparison and tensor relation

complete_proofs.scope: Single-edge BMP recursion, unique free basis (1,1),(a,0), and global versus local reduced Hilbert polynomials.
The A2 interval [e,s1s2]: all edge labels, boundary image R/(ab), rank-one vertex stalks, unique four-parameter global section basis, Hilbert polynomial 1+2t+t^2.
Rank-one R tensor_{R^s} R -> moment-graph sections: balanced map, two bimodule actions, multiplicativity, graded inverse by even/odd decomposition.
Rank-one Soergel tensor-square isomorphism with explicit inverse and both unshifted and normalized grading conventions.

deepening.boundary: Only the stated one-edge and four-vertex examples and the rank-one tensor model are proved. No general Coxeter KL/IH identification, Hodge proof or positive-characteristic claim.

limitations: Section 6 now has complete one-edge and A2 diamond BMP calculations plus the rank-one Soergel comparison/tensor relation. Arbitrary Coxeter realizations, higher-rank Soergel decomposition, general KL identification and section 9 positive-characteristic parity theory remain unproved or unintegrated.

No construction of geometric intersection complexes, equivariant cohomology, or proof of the Hodge-Riemann relations; the notes use the purely algebraic construction with explicitly labelled deep inputs.

The survey itself cites forthcoming work [15,16] for the canonical identification between its equivariant sheaf construction and previously constructed matroid IH; those unavailable proofs were not claimed as read.
The reversed displayed monotonicity inequality (8.1) was detected and not copied; this task does not supply a separate corrected monotonicity theorem.
Conjecture nodes record the report's questions, not an independently exhaustive current-literature status review.

papers.title: Totally Positive Toeplitz Matrices: Classical and Modern
papers.license: Official SIAM publication: CC BY 4.0; arXiv v3 uses arXiv nonexclusive-distrib/1.0, not CC BY.

coverage.read_version: arXiv:2509.25163v3 (2025-10-13), 20 PDF pages; exact title/authors/venue/pages/license and selected equations cross-checked against SIAM HTML.
coverage.read_body: All body sections 1-3, PDF pp. 1-18; bibliography pp. 18-20 inspected, not a reading of all references.
integrated_sections: 1.1: Edrei classification including zero parameters and gamma
2.1-2.2: minors, finite parametrization, standard coordinates, quiver criterion
2.4: standard-truncation special case of Theorem 2.7 with its logarithmic-average proof; quantum-parameter corollary; exponential example
2.5: explicit divisor functions and their two endpoint limits from Lemma 2.13 and Corollary 2.14
2.6: multiplication-table uniqueness with explicit positive-arrow hypothesis and conditional proof route
3.1-3.2: min-plus operations, min-ideal fillings, corrected weight indices and finite bijection
3.4: combinatorial part of Theorem 3.16 with an independent rectangle proof
3.5: Theorem 3.18 under explicit uniform triangular-coordinate convergence and finite row/column limits, with error estimate
proof_detail: 01DB gives the truncation case completely conditional on Edrei's coordinate-ratio theorem.
01DL proves divisor limits by a fixed finite sum.
01DI labels the Edrei-based uniqueness argument as a proof route.
01DT proves the combinatorial infinite parameterization directly, but does not prove lifting to positive functions.
01DV gives the uniform-error estimate for tropical weight limits.
01DQ independently solves the rank-two weight inversion.

sections: 2.3: S3 divided differences, standard-elementary quantization and an explicit localized 3x3 Toeplitz algebra isomorphism
2.5: finite-polynomial standard-truncation degeneration and the six S3 two-end examples

complete_proofs.scope: Polynomial divided-difference nilpotence, distant commutation, twisted Leibniz rule and full three-variable braid calculation.
All six S3 classical Schubert polynomials by divided differences and their unimodular integer basis change.
All six S3 quantum Schubert polynomials by explicit standard-elementary expansion; ordinary divided differences do not supply the quantum recursion.
Complete 3x3 Toeplitz minor enumeration, exact total-positivity region and four quantum/divisor parameter formulas.
Isomorphism of explicitly defined localized polynomial rings, including invertibility of U,V, all defining relations and two-sided inverse without dividing by x1. Not the geometric Peterson theorem.
All six rational images and strict positivity on a>0, 0<b<a^2, by substitution and elementary simplification.

deepening.boundary: Finite polynomial and algebra calculations are proved; geometric Schubert-class identification, general Peterson theory and stable geometric interpretation remain named external inputs. Actual standard truncations only.

limitations: The previously omitted quantum/Schubert branch now includes S3 polynomial constructions, complete finite Toeplitz identities and an algebraic rank-two localized-ring isomorphism. Thoma/Vershik-Kerov theory, general geometric Schubert/Peterson and mirror identifications, general Theorem 2.16 beyond the explicitly conditional finite-polynomial deduction, and strong/weak topology lifting remain unproved or unintegrated.

Theorems 2.7 and Corollary 2.14 are only integrated for actual truncations of one infinite matrix; arbitrary approximating matrices are not claimed. The manuscript proof switches from coefficient-space closeness to uniform logarithmic standard-coordinate control, which is not justified merely by coordinatewise convergence.
The positive-parameter assumption is retained for reciprocal/logarithmic limits; the exponential example is handled separately.
The standard weight formula is corrected from the root labelling in Remark 3.2 and the diagonal-minor formula, not copied with the printed off-by-one indices.
Finite parameterization and Edrei ratio limits are stated as theorem inputs; their original analytic/quantum-cohomological proofs are not reproduced.
The SIAM and KCL PDF endpoints returned HTTP 403 to curl; exact report PDF was downloaded from arXiv instead. No older paper substituted.

complete_proofs.scope: Single-edge BMP recursion, unique free basis (1,1),(a,0), and global versus local reduced Hilbert polynomials.
The A2 interval [e,s1s2]: all edge labels, boundary image R/(ab), rank-one vertex stalks, unique four-parameter global section basis, Hilbert polynomial 1+2t+t^2.
Rank-one R tensor_{R^s} R -> moment-graph sections: balanced map, two bimodule actions, multiplicativity, graded inverse by even/odd decomposition.
Rank-one Soergel tensor-square isomorphism with explicit inverse and both unshifted and normalized grading conventions.
Polynomial divided-difference nilpotence, distant commutation, twisted Leibniz rule and full three-variable braid calculation.
All six S3 classical Schubert polynomials by divided differences and their unimodular integer basis change.
All six S3 quantum Schubert polynomials by explicit standard-elementary expansion; ordinary divided differences do not supply the quantum recursion.
Complete 3x3 Toeplitz minor enumeration, exact total-positivity region and four quantum/divisor parameter formulas.
Isomorphism of explicitly defined localized polynomial rings, including invertibility of U,V, all defining relations and two-sided inverse without dividing by x1. Not the geometric Peterson theorem.
All six rational images and strict positivity on a>0, 0<b<a^2, by substitution and elementary simplification.

limitations: No separate integration of the Coxeter/moment-graph/Soergel branch in section 6 or positive-characteristic parity theory in section 9.

No construction of geometric intersection complexes, equivariant cohomology, or proof of the Hodge-Riemann relations; the notes use the purely algebraic construction with explicitly labelled deep inputs.

The survey itself cites forthcoming work [15,16] for the canonical identification between its equivariant sheaf construction and previously constructed matroid IH; those unavailable proofs were not claimed as read.
The reversed displayed monotonicity inequality (8.1) was detected and not copied; this task does not supply a separate corrected monotonicity theorem.
Conjecture nodes record the report's questions, not an independently exhaustive current-literature status review.

Thoma/Vershik-Kerov representation theory, general quantum Schubert polynomial limit Theorem 2.16, Peterson-ring and mirror-symmetry identifications, and the strong/weak topology lifting theorems are read but not separately integrated.

Theorems 2.7 and Corollary 2.14 are only integrated for actual truncations of one infinite matrix; arbitrary approximating matrices are not claimed. The manuscript proof switches from coefficient-space closeness to uniform logarithmic standard-coordinate control, which is not justified merely by coordinatewise convergence.
The positive-parameter assumption is retained for reciprocal/logarithmic limits; the exponential example is handled separately.
The standard weight formula is corrected from the root labelling in Remark 3.2 and the diagonal-minor formula, not copied with the printed off-by-one indices.
Finite parameterization and Edrei ratio limits are stated as theorem inputs; their original analytic/quantum-cohomological proofs are not reproduced.
The SIAM and KCL PDF endpoints returned HTTP 403 to curl; exact report PDF was downloaded from arXiv instead. No older paper substituted.
